title: CIVICLEDGER reproducible case dossier

snapshot.title: CIVICLEDGER
snapshot.scope: NRC-awarded prime contract transactions; all sectors; action dates 2021-10-01 through 2024-09-30
caveats: Obligations are commitments, not cash outlays; outlay fields are unavailable here.
All three fiscal years are complete calendar windows as of this retrieval; the source can revise historical records.
Award timelines and first/last observation are truncated to this cohort, not award or supplier lifetime.
No misconduct labels or fraud-detection accuracy; patterns are contextual review candidates.
Names and parent reports are observed attributes. A UEI identifies a legal entity, not necessarily an independent corporate group.
Raw full-field archives remain local. 4 contact-bearing descriptions are omitted from this public snapshot.
unavailable: Tender notice dates and tender duration

privacy_transformations.rule: Whole description omitted when email address or North American telephone pattern is detected; raw original unchanged.

snapshot.concentration_convention: Positive recipient-year net obligation shares, HHI 0–10000; signed net flows always retained separately.

selection.scope: Fixed case evidence uses the complete FY2022–FY2024 cohort, independent of explorer filters.

net.title: Net obligations
net.formula: Σ federal_action_obligation for all transactions in the selected fiscal-year cohort, including negative values.
net.sql:
SELECT fiscal_year, SUM(obligation) AS net_obligations
FROM fact_transactions
WHERE fiscal_year = :fiscal_year
GROUP BY fiscal_year;
net.caveat: Obligations are legally binding commitments. They are not cash outlays, award ceilings, or the sum of repeated award summaries. Negative obligations can reflect legitimate cancellations, adjustments, and closeouts.

awards.title: Distinct awards
awards.formula: COUNT(DISTINCT award_id) among selected transactions. An award can have many modifications and can appear in several fiscal years.
awards.caveat: An award count does not measure contracts newly signed in the year. Existing awards with modifications are included.

recipients.title: Identified recipients
recipients.formula: COUNT(DISTINCT recipient_id) among selected transactions. Prefer UEI, then source identifier, then an explicitly unresolved record key.
recipients.caveat: Different legal recipients can share a parent company. A name is not a reliable unique identifier. Grouping by parents answers a different concentration question.

hhi.title: Supplier concentration · HHI
hhi.formula: HHI = 10,000 × Σ (supplier positive-net share)². First sum signed obligations by recipient in the selected window; use max(recipient net balance,0) as the concentration weight.
hhi.caveat: Concentration is descriptive. It can reflect specialized requirements, framework vehicles, or a narrow cohort. It is not a finding about misconduct. HHI ranges from 0 to 10,000 for nonnegative shares.

competition.title: Reported competition
competition.formula: Transaction counts by source competition classification. Missing or unknown codes remain a separate denominator category.
competition.sql:
SELECT CASE WHEN competition_code IN ('A','D','F') THEN 'competed'
 WHEN competition_code IN ('B','C','G','NDO') THEN 'noncompetitive'
 ELSE 'unknown' END AS status, COUNT(*) AS transactions
FROM fact_transactions
WHERE fiscal_year = :fiscal_year
GROUP BY status;
competition.caveat: Reported competition is an administrative field, not a reconstruction of bids. Modifications often inherit award characteristics. A noncompetitive action may have lawful statutory justification.

yearend.title: September share
yearend.formula: Positive obligations dated in September ÷ positive obligations in the selected fiscal-year cohort.
yearend.sql:
SELECT fiscal_year,
  SUM(CASE WHEN MONTH(action_date)=9 THEN GREATEST(obligation,0) ELSE 0 END)
  / NULLIF(SUM(GREATEST(obligation,0)),0) AS september_share
FROM fact_transactions GROUP BY fiscal_year;
yearend.caveat: Fiscal years end September 30. Budget timing, planned renewals, reporting delays, and program schedules can explain a September peak. Timing alone does not establish waste or wrongdoing.

annual.title: Annual obligations
annual.formula: Net transaction obligations grouped by federal fiscal year (October 1 through September 30).
annual.sql:
SELECT fiscal_year, SUM(obligation) AS net_obligations,
  SUM(GREATEST(obligation,0)) AS positive_obligations,
  SUM(LEAST(obligation,0)) AS deobligations
FROM fact_transactions GROUP BY fiscal_year ORDER BY fiscal_year;
annual.caveat: A fiscal-year trend mixes award starts, continuing work, modifications, and deobligations. No causal claim follows from this descriptive time series.

peers.title: Peer-group comparison
peers.formula: Compare within the selected fiscal-year window and the first three digits of the reported NAICS industry code. Compute positive-net recipient shares within each peer group.
peers.sql:
WITH suppliers AS (
 SELECT fiscal_year, LEFT(naics,3) AS naics, recipient_id,
 GREATEST(SUM(obligation),0) AS positive
 FROM fact_transactions GROUP BY ALL
), shares AS (
 SELECT *, positive / SUM(positive) OVER (PARTITION BY fiscal_year,naics) AS share
 FROM suppliers
)
SELECT fiscal_year, naics, COUNT(*) AS recipients,
 10000*SUM(share*share) AS hhi
FROM shares GROUP BY fiscal_year,naics;
peers.caveat: NAICS categories are broad industry labels, not fully interchangeable markets. Small peer groups produce unstable comparisons. Size, technical specialization, and contract vehicles can explain differences.

top.title: Recipient funding shares
top.formula: For each recipient, sum signed transaction obligations, take max(net balance,0), then divide by the sum of positive recipient net balances. Negative adjustments remain in every net total.
top.sql:
SELECT recipient_id, ARG_MAX(recipient_name,action_date) AS recipient_name,
 SUM(obligation) AS net_obligations,
 GREATEST(SUM(obligation),0) AS concentration_weight,
 COUNT(DISTINCT award_id) AS awards
FROM fact_transactions
WHERE fiscal_year = :fiscal_year
GROUP BY recipient_id
ORDER BY concentration_weight DESC;
top.caveat: Large totals are not a risk ranking. Prime recipients may contract with other organizations, and the data do not measure ultimate economic benefit.

flow.title: Agency → award → recipient
flow.formula: Selected agency transaction obligations are grouped by award_id and attributed to the recipient reported on each action. Award summary totals are never added across modifications.
flow.sql:
SELECT agency_name, award_id, recipient_id,
 SUM(obligation) AS net_obligations, COUNT(*) AS actions
FROM fact_transactions
WHERE fiscal_year = :fiscal_year
GROUP BY agency_name,award_id,recipient_id;
flow.caveat: The explorer shows prime-award commitments for the bounded cohort. It does not show all government spending, cash paid, or complete subcontracting relationships.

case.title: A negative action is part of the accounting
case.question: What changes when reductions in commitments are retained?
case.selection: Most negative individual action obligation in the cohort.
case.metric_label: signed obligation on the selected modification
case.formula: min(federal_action_obligation) across all cohort actions; accounting identity: net = positive + negative obligations
case.sql: select transaction_id, obligation from fact_transactions where obligation<0 order by obligation limit 1;
case.interpretation: A deobligation reduces a prior commitment. It must remain in net totals and timelines. Its size alone cannot establish whether the underlying activity was appropriate.
case.uncertainty: The observation window excludes earlier actions. Cumulative amounts begin at the window boundary, not contract inception.
case.finding: A deobligation reduces a prior commitment. It must remain in net totals and timelines. Its size alone cannot establish whether the underlying activity was appropriate.
case.denominator_text: 4,683 transaction actions. Most negative individual action obligation in the cohort.

entity_scenario_scope: One conditional pair preview at a time; all other components remain unresolved. Conditional mean metrics and modal sampled rankings are not a joint resolved partition.
